fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. David says they will "…shred my soul like a lion and tear me to pieces…" (Psalm 7:2). A lion is a scary picture, and tearing to pieces comes right along with it. Just before that, he says, "…I take refuge in You…" (Psalm 7:1).
Yes, baker. David says, "…if I have rewarded my ally with evil…" (Psalm 7:4). He puts it on his list right next to plundering his foe without cause. I think he wants God to look at all of it.
It's actually on the list, friend. David says, "…if I have rewarded my ally with evil…" (Psalm 7:4). The next item is plundering his foe without cause. Two items sit in that one verse.

That's it, baker. David says, "…then may my enemy pursue me and overtake me; may he trample me to the ground and leave my honor in the dust." (Psalm 7:5). He names the penalty himself, if he has done these things. Not many of us would sign that paper.

Good heart, baker, but that's not what David says. He says that if he's done these things, "…may my enemy pursue me and overtake me; may he trample me to the ground and leave my honor in the dust." (Psalm 7:5). He's not asking to be let off the hook. I think he's showing how sure he is.

Peace would be nice, baker, but that's not the request. David says, "Awake, my God, and ordain judgment." (Psalm 7:6). He asks God to ordain judgment, and he mentions the fury of his enemies in the same breath.
Right, baker. David asks, "vindicate me, O LORD, according to my righteousness and integrity." (Psalm 7:8). Righteousness and integrity are the words he uses. Rank never comes up in that ask.
That's right, baker. David calls Him the "…righteous God who searches hearts and minds." (Psalm 7:9). What he names is what's inside: hearts and minds.

Close to David's world, friend, but not here. Jonathan, who made a covenant with David (1 Samuel 18:3), isn't named in this verse. David says, "My shield is with God, who saves the upright in heart." (Psalm 7:10).
Yes, baker. David says the wicked man "…conceives trouble and births falsehood." (Psalm 7:14). What he births is falsehood. That's the picture.
That's a nice guess, baker, but the picture goes further. David says he "…conceives trouble and births falsehood." (Psalm 7:14). The trouble is conceived, and falsehood is what he births.
Patience is a nice word, baker, but David uses a different one. He says, "I will thank the LORD for His righteousness…" (Psalm 7:17). He has already called God righteous earlier in this psalm.
